## Application-level inputs

Call `predict(pdat, idat=None, batch_size=128)` with a pandas DataFrame containing
one application per `id`. Required columns are `id`, `tan_app` (applied total
ammoniacal nitrogen, kg N/ha), and `app_method`. Use positive applied TAN.
Identifiers must be consistent between `pdat` and `idat`.

The following tables are generated from the parameters shipped with the installed
release. Access to these internal objects is used for documentation only; the
public interface is `from nh3pred import predict`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from nh3pred.preprocessing import (
    categorial_correspondances, default_values, public_fertiliser_categories,
)

print("| Input | Accepted categories (case-sensitive) | Default |")
print("|---|---|---|")
for name in ["app_method", "incorp", "till", "fer_origin", "fer_forme",
             "fer_trt1", "fer_trt2", "crop", "soil_type"]:
    categories = public_fertiliser_categories.get(
        name, set(categorial_correspondances[name])
    )
    if name == "crop":
        categories = set(categories) - {"unknown"}
    values = ", ".join(f"`{value}`" for value in sorted(categories))
    default = "required" if name == "app_method" else str(default_values[name])
    print(f"| `{name}` | {values} | {default} |")
```

Application methods are broadcast (`bc`), band spreading/trailing hose (`bsth`),
trailing shoe (`ts`), open slot (`os`), closed slot (`cs`) and pressurised
injection (`pi`). Origins include cattle (`cat`), pig (`pig`), concentrate
(`conc`), mixed (`mix`) and other (`other`). Treatments are represented by two
separate columns: `fer_trt1` and `fer_trt2`. `meas_tech` and `fer_trt3` are
internal model variables and are rejected as public inputs.

| Numeric input | Unit | Default or missing-value rule |
|---|---|---|
| `app_rate` | t/ha | 20.457020689428806 + 0.25233812374128917 × `tan_app` |
| `fer_dm` | % | 6.59 |
| `fer_ph` | pH | 7.3 |
| `crop_z` | cm | 10 for a crop; not applicable for bare soil |
| `time_incorp` | h | 0.05 for incorporation; not applicable for `none` |
| `furrow_z` | cm | Missing unless supplied |
| `soil_water` | volumetric fraction | 0.2715 |
| `soil_ph` | pH | 6.5 |
| `soil_dens` | g/cm³ | 1.14 |
| `soil_oc` | % | 3.49 |

Supply measured values where possible. Defaults are not substitutes for site
characterisation. Selecting a solid fertilizer does not automatically adjust
dry matter or produce a low-dry-matter warning. The package does not validate
every physical range or scientifically plausible combination of predictors.

## Time and weather

Optional `idat` has one row per time point and application, with `id` and `ct`
(hours since application). Supply strictly increasing positive times for each
application, without duplicates. Weather inputs are `air_temp` (°C), `wind_2m`
(m/s at 2 m), and `rain_rate` (mm/h).

If `idat` is omitted, predictions use 29 default time points: 2, 4, then every
4 hours through 48 h, followed by every 12 hours through 240 h. Missing weather
columns receive the bundled default profiles for air temperature and wind,
and zero rain. Profiles are linearly interpolated at the requested times;
outside their time range, endpoint values are held constant. Missing entries
in an existing weather column retain the model's missing-value representation.
`rain_cum` is computed from interval durations and `rain_rate`; a supplied
`rain_cum` column is overwritten.

```{python}
import pandas as pd
from nh3pred import predict

reference_pdat = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1], "tan_app": [100.0], "app_method": ["bc"]})
reference_idat = pd.DataFrame({
    "id": [1, 1, 1], "ct": [2.0, 24.0, 48.0],
    "air_temp": [12.0, 15.0, 13.0], "wind_2m": [2.0, 3.0, 2.0],
    "rain_rate": [0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
})
predict(reference_pdat, reference_idat)[["id", "ct", "prediction_ecum", "prediction_erel"]]
```

## Output and interpretation

`prediction_ecum` is cumulative NH$_3$ emission in kg N/ha; `prediction_erel` is
the fraction of applied TAN emitted (not a percentage). All numeric output
columns, including copied inputs, are rounded to two decimals. Computation uses
unrounded inputs. The reservoir model constrains cumulative emissions to be
non-decreasing and at most the applied TAN. Long-horizon predictions and unusual
input combinations remain extrapolations, not validated field forecasts.
